title: Tuna Pasta Bake
subtitle: British classic with a cheesy white sauce
excerpt: Pasta, tinned tuna, and sweetcorn in a creamy white sauce, topped with a bubbling cheese crust. This is the British kitchen staple done properly: a proper bechamel rather than soup from a tin, and a generous amount of cheese on top.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tuna pasta bake is one of the great British store-cupboard dishes, popular from the 1970s onwards when tinned tuna became widely available and affordable. The original version often used condensed cream of mushroom soup as the sauce, but this version uses a proper bechamel for a richer, better-flavoured result. It is a weekly fixture in millions of British households.

recipeTools.notes: For the pasta and the white sauce.

content.text: Cook the pasta just short of al dente: it will continue cooking in the oven. A properly made bechamel from butter, flour, and milk is much better than tinned soup and takes only 10 minutes. Season the sauce generously with salt, pepper, and mustard before adding the tuna and sweetcorn.
Cook the penne in salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain and set aside.

Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes. Add the milk in a slow stream, whisking constantly. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring, and cook for 5 minutes until thick and smooth. Remove from the heat. Add two-thirds of the cheese and the mustard. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Fold the drained pasta, tuna, sweetcorn, and spring onions into the cheese sauce. Pour into a baking dish. Scatter the remaining cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling and the sauce is hot throughout. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
